newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Alfonsin in hospital for heart spasm.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Alfonsin in hospital for heart spasm.

text.p: Argentine former President Raul Alfonsin was admitted to the coronary unit of a Buenos Aires hospital on Friday after a routine check detected heart problems, local television and news agencies reported.
But his aides said the 69-year-old Radical Party leader, who was Argentina's first democratic president after military dictatorship ended in 1983, was not in serious danger.

Alfonsin's spokesman Simon Lazara told the state news agency Telam that Alfonsin went to the Italian Hospital for a routine monthly check-up but was told he would have to stay under observation until Saturday because of a "heart spasm."
"He's likely to be discharged tomorrow," said Lazara.
After losing an election to Peronist Carlos Menem in 1989, Alfonsin was forced by economic disarray to leave office six months before his term ended.
He is no longer head of the Radical Party, but is still one of its most powerful figures and has recently talked of making another bid for the Argentine presidency in 1999.
Famed for his oratory, Alfonsin drew a crowd of 30,000 to a Buenos Aires soccer stadium in November for a rally against the "neo-conservative" policies applied by Menem's government.
